newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BLACK CONTROL SEEN OPENING AFRICA TO JCI.
newsitem.headline: BLACK CONTROL SEEN OPENING AFRICA TO JCI.

text.p: Now ruled by a black business consortium, South African mining house JCI Ltd will be able to venture more easily into Africa than before, new controlling stakeholders African Mining Group said on Thursday.
"With JCI being the first truly African mining house we will be in a position to access... that, given its history, JCI couldn't," African Mining Group (AMG) chairman Reuel Khosa said.

Khosa was speaking at a ceremony whereby Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd signed over its controlling 34.9 percent stake in JCI to AMG. The signing follows an earlier announcement on Tuesday that AMG had won the bidding for Anglo's stake.
AMG Deputy chairman Mzi Khumalo said that JCI's new rulers aimed to benefit the group by "optimising relationships".
He said that AMG, a black empowerment consortium, planned to make JCI the most profitable mining company in the world.
AMG is led by Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd .
Anglo sold its stake for 54.50 rand per share or 2.88 billion rand. The purchase would take effect from January 1, 1997, the companies said in a joint statement on Thursday.
A further 1.3 percent of JCI's issued share capital will be made available through a retail offer to an independent trust set up for members of the black community over four months.
The consortium would have the right of first refusal for a period of five years to purchase the remaining 13 percent stake held by Anglo American and its affiliate De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd.

JCI's board of directors would be reconstituted to comprise 14 members, of whom seven members would be nominated by the consortium, including the chairman, while Anglo American would have certain minority protection rights.
The agreement is subject to the fulfilment of certain suspensive conditions, including a due diligence investigation which will last until February 28, 1997.
During this time the consortium would also finalise the funding required for the purchase of the JCI shares.
"We have already started talking to a number of financial institutions, both local and abroad and some of them are very positive," AMG's Khosa said.
The consortium was of the opinion that the purchase price represented a discount to the fair value of JCI.
JCI shares closed on Thursday at 47.75 rand.

The consortium includes African Renaissance Holdings, Co-ordinated Network Investments (Pty) Ltd, Corridor Development Corporation, Khotso Investments (Pty) Ltd, Northern Corporate Investment Holdings (Pty) Ltd, Thebe Investment Corp (Pty) Ltd and Women's Development Bank Investment Holdings Ltd.
